question_text: Consider an LED based on a direct bandgap semiconductor material with energy bandgap 1.3 eV. Given: Plank’s constant, \(h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\) J s and speed of light in free space is \(3 \times 10^8\) m s\(^{-1}\). In which of the following wavelength ranges the LED will NOT emit?

Let the relevant bandwidth (\(B\)) of a digital communication system be 1 MHz and \(kT = -174\) dBm/Hz, where \(k\) is Boltzmann’s constant and ‘\(T\)’ is equivalent noise temperature of the receiver. The power (\(S\)) of signal received through an additive Gaussian channel is \(-80\) dBm. Which of the following options is/are TRUE about Shannon capacity (\(C\)) of the channel?

Consider the four-variable Boolean function,
\(f(w,x,y,z) = \sum m(0,2,5,7,8,10,13,14,15)\) with ‘\(w\)’ as MSB and ‘\(z\)’ as LSB.
Which of the following expressions is/are the valid form(s) of \(f(w,x,y,z)\)?

Consider a real, narrowband signal \(x(t) = A(t)\cos[2\pi f_c t + \theta(t)]\) where the maximum frequency components of \(A(t)\) and \(\theta(t)\) are \(f_M\) and \(f_c\) (\(= 1000 f_M\)), respectively. Which of the following statements is/are correct for \(-\infty < t < \infty\)?

options.text: \(x(t)\) represents a PSK modulated signal for suitable choices of \(A(t)\) and \(\theta(t)\).
\(x(t)\) represents an amplitude modulated signal for suitable choices of \(A(t)\) and \(\theta(t)\).
\(x(t)\) represents a band-limited Gaussian noise process.
\(x(t)\) never represents a narrowband FM signal.

question_text: Let \(x_1(t) = \cos(2\pi n t)\) and \(x_2(t) = 2\sin(4\pi n t)\) represent two sinusoids for a positive integer \(n\) and \(-\infty < t < \infty\). Which of the following statements about \(x_1(t)\) and \(x_2(t)\) is/are valid?

options.text: \(x_1(t)\) and \(x_2(t)\) are orthogonal to each other over \(0 \le t < 1/n\).
\(x_1(t)\) and \(x_2(t)\) are orthonormal to each other over \(0 \le t < 1/n\).
\(x_1(t)\) and \(x_2(t)\) are non-orthogonal to each other over \(0 \le t < 1/(2n)\).
